title: Thomas Massie Moves to Force Vote on Impeaching Pete Hegseth
partialText: Representative Thomas Massie, Republican of Kentucky, set in motion a vote that must occur by Wednesday. If the House approves the charges, it will prompt a Senate trial.

title: Trump Veers Back Into Claims of Rigged Election, Questioning Midterm Results
partialText: President Trump, who initially said he would accept the midterm results, renewed his unsubstantiated claims that voting was manipulated.

title: Congress Has Reined In the Presidency Before. Here’s How to Do It.
partialText: History tells us that constitutional oversight can be a powerful tool — if wielded correctly.

title: U.S. Commerce Dept. Inquiry Into Megaspeed Was Halted After Nvidia Intervention
partialText: An investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company that was buying advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, was transferred to the Justice Department after a top Nvidia executive reached out to Commerce Department officials.

title: A.I. Fueled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Elite Status, but Scandal Followed
partialText: As chips became essential components for A.I., executives like Nvidia’s Jensen Huang saw their personal wealth and profiles soar in a way the industry has not experienced before.

title: Democrats Demand Answers on Trump’s A.I. Policy Amid Spy Plot
partialText: Congressional leaders raise concerns in a letter as Nvidia investigates its chief executive’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Drops After Investigation Into CEO Jensen Huang
partialText: The chip maker’s shares fell sharply after its C.E.O., Jensen Huang, admitted to a relationship with a businesswoman suspected of spying for China.

title: An Anti-Trump Protest. Police Threats. Inside a Rift in Diabetes Research.
partialText: It began with a protest at an American Diabetes Association conference. Now a resulting boycott has caused a scientific slowdown, with no end in sight.

title: Could the Voter Backlash Against A.I. Actually Help the Economy?
partialText: Voter backlash could threaten the data center boom. Some economists think that could be a good thing.

title: What Is Congress’s Plan to Speed Up Energy Permits?
partialText: The sprawling bill, which has divided Democrats, would overhaul major environmental laws to streamline the permitting process.

title: For Years, She Felt Awful. Her Flexible Joints Held a Clue.
partialText: Many people with hypermobility disorders spend years trying to figure out what’s wrong. Online communities are helping them connect the dots.

title: Supreme Court Allows Construction of Trump’s Border Wall in Big Bend
partialText: The administration had asked the court to permit construction of a border wall in southwestern Texas, including areas within a national park.

title: Why Colorado Is at the Epicenter of So Many Supreme Court Clashes
partialText: In three recent cases, the conservative-dominated bench has ruled against the state and in favor of the rights of Christian business owners.

title: A Decade After Henry Worsley Died in Antarctica, His Son Tries to Reach the South Pole
partialText: A decade after Max Worsley’s father died crossing the continent, he embarks this month on his own journey into the lonely land his father loved.

title: Russell Brand Sentenced to 10 and a Half Years in Prison for Rape
partialText: A London judge said the former comedy star, who was convicted of rape and sexual assault last week, had shown a “casual, arrogant disregard” for women’s wishes.

title: Megyn Kelly, Elon Musk and Others Defend Russell Brand After Rape Conviction
partialText: The former star, whom a British judge sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison on Monday, became an anti-establishment flag-bearer through conspiracy-minded commentary.

title: In a Democratic Wave, Even the Long Shots Defied the Odds
partialText: A handful of Democrats scored improbable victories in races against Republican incumbents who were favored to win.

title: Progressives Defied Their Party and Won Big. They Still Feel Ignored.
partialText: As Democrats prepare to take power in Congress, some centrists are brushing off the victories of left-wing candidates. The left is pushing back.

title: ‘Talafreako’ Is, Accidentally, the Campaign Song of the Moment
partialText: An impromptu song by a Texas rapper has helped immortalize the frisky nickname of Senator-elect James Talarico.

title: At 87, Senfronia Thompson is Poised to Become the First Woman to Lead the Texas House
partialText: At 87, Senfronia Thompson of Houston is poised to become the first woman, and Black lawmaker, to lead the Texas House.

title: Her Death From Dengue May Signal That the Disease Is Here to Stay
partialText: In the past, Americans were infected with dengue after being bitten by mosquitoes while traveling. But now, most of the current transmission is from local mosquitoes.

title: M. John Harrison’s ‘The End of Everything’ Wins Booker Prize
partialText: M. John Harrison’s dystopian tale “The End of Everything” beat out higher profile books by Marlon James, Elizabeth Strout and Douglas Stuart.

title: Book Review: ‘The End of Everything,’ by M. John Harrison
partialText: Very little is clear in M. John Harrison’s Booker-nominated novel “The End of Everything,” except that nothing is as it seems.

title: Trump Has Found His New Roy Cohn in Stephen Miller
partialText: Stephen Miller is the wartime consigliere Trump always wanted.

title: Paulina Porizkova: Why I Now Call Myself a Feminist
partialText: The former model looks back at what she wrote in The Times about feminism nine years ago.

title: Judge Denies Request to Throw Out Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Charges
partialText: The judge also declined to investigate the lone juror who wanted to convict Ms. Clancy, saying it would invade his privacy and deter others from serving on juries.
